extracted.intended_audience: AQA examiners and teachers marking GCSE English Language (Paper 1); useful to students
extracted.subtask_description: Mark scheme for AQA GCSE English Language Paper 1 (Explorations in creative reading and writing) giving assessment objectives, level-based grade descriptors, and detailed question-by-question marking guidance for examiners and teachers.

rubrics_metrics.name: General marking principle
rubrics_metrics.description: The information provided for each question is intended to be a guide to the kind of answers anticipated and is neither exhaustive nor prescriptive. All appropriate responses should be given credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should treat the indicative content as guidance only; credit any valid response that meets the question's focus. An answer which contains nothing of relevance must be awarded no marks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of literary/linguistic terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Where literary or linguistic terms appear in the Mark Scheme, they do so generally for the sake of brevity. Knowledge of such terms, other than those given in the specification, is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, when determining the level of response, examiners should take into account instances where the student uses these terms effectively to aid clarity and precision of the argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level of response marking instructions (general procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Level of response mark schemes are broken down into four levels. There are two, four, five or six marks in each level; dependent upon question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step 1: Determine a level — start at the lowest level and 'ladder' up until the answer meets the descriptor. Step 2: Determine a mark — once a level is assigned, decide the mark within that level. To achieve full marks in a level, students should meet all of the skills descriptors. Students achieving marks at the bottom of a level will ideally have met all of the skills descriptors of the previous level and at least one of the skills descriptors in that level. Level 0: no marks (no relevant material).

rubrics_metrics.name: AO1
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and interpret explicit and implicit information and ideas. Select and synthesise evidence from different texts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess accurate identification and selection of textual information; applied in questions that require retrieval and synthesis of text-based facts/ideas (e.g. Q1).

rubrics_metrics.name: AO2
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain, comment on and analyse how writers use language and structure to achieve effects and influence readers, using relevant subject terminology to support their views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers analysis of words/phrases/language features/techniques/sentence forms and structural features at whole-text, paragraph and sentence levels. Marked using level descriptors from simple comment (Level 1) to detailed, perceptive analysis (Level 4). Examiners should reward selection of judicious textual detail and accurate subject terminology.

rubrics_metrics.name: AO3
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare writers’ ideas and perspectives, as well as how these are conveyed, across two or more texts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: AO3 is not assessed on this paper (N/A for Paper 1 in this mark scheme).

rubrics_metrics.name: AO4
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate texts critically and support this with appropriate textual references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses critical evaluation and understanding of writers' methods; levelled from simple/limited evaluation (Level 1) to perceptive, detailed evaluation (Level 4). Examiners should look for perceptive judgement, a judicious range of textual detail and development of a convincing response to the focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: AO5
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicate clearly, effectively and imaginatively, selecting and adapting tone, style and register for different forms, purposes and audiences. Organise information and ideas, using structural and grammatical features to support coherence and cohesion of texts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess content and organisation in the creative writing task. Level descriptors distinguish between simple/limited writing (Level 1) and compelling, convincing writing with extensive ambitious vocabulary and inventive structural features (Level 4).

rubrics_metrics.name: AO6
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates must use a range of vocabulary and sentence structures for clarity, purpose and effect, with accurate spelling and punctuation. (This requirement must constitute 20% of the marks for each specification as a whole).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AO6 marks technical accuracy: sentence demarcation, range and accuracy of punctuation, variety of sentence forms, control of Standard English and grammatical structures, and accuracy of spelling (including ambitious vocabulary). Levelled from limited/basic accuracy (Level 1) to consistently secure and wide-range, accurate use (Level 4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment objectives mapped to paper sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Which Assessment Objectives are assessed in each section of Paper 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section A (Reading) assesses AO1 and AO2 and AO4 (AO3 is N/A). Section B (Writing) assesses AO5 and AO6. Examiners should apply the relevant AOs when marking each question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q1: Reading retrieval (List four things) — AO1
rubrics_metrics.description: Read again the first part of the Source from lines 1 to 7. List four things from this part of the Source about the boy. [4 marks]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give 1 mark for each point about the boy. Responses must be true and drawn only from lines 1 to 7 of the text. Responses must relate to the boy. Students may quote or paraphrase. A paraphrased response covering more than one point should be credited for each point made — though paraphrased responses must demonstrate evidence of identification of information that is specific to the focus of the question as required by AO1. Responses that copy the whole section verbatim should not be credited any marks as this does not provide evidence of identification specific to the focus. Indicative content list provided (e.g. he liked evening time the best; he felt able to slow time down; he collected broken green glass; he built little houses etc.) but is not exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q2: Language analysis (How does the writer use language?) — AO2
rubrics_metrics.description: Look in detail at an extract. How does the writer use language here to describe the boy playing in the evening? You could include words/phrases, language features and techniques, sentence forms. [8 marks]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked by levels: Level 4 (7–8 marks) detailed, perceptive analysis: analyses effects, selects a judicious range of detail, sophisticated and accurate subject terminology; Level 3 (5–6) clear explanation; Level 2 (3–4) some understanding; Level 1 (1–2) simple limited comment; Level 0 no marks. Indicative content examples: use of sibilance to create unease ('fragments','glass','shattered'), listing and action verbs to show imaginative creation ('making houses, balancing roofs, building towers'), harsh crisp sounds ('sunlight','caught','glinted') to foreshadow, references to time and encroaching darkness ('nine chimes','the shadows were growing'), similes ('like a tall thin man','shattered marbles'), subject terminology should be used where appropriate. Exemplar commentary passages provided as guidance on expected depth at each level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q3: Structure analysis (How has the writer structured the text?) — AO2
rubrics_metrics.description: How has the writer structured the text to interest you as a reader? Consider initial focus, how/why the focus changes, other structural features. [8 marks]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked by levels: Level 4 (7–8) perceptive, detailed analysis of structural features; Level 3 (5–6) clear explanation; Level 2 (3–4) some understanding/comment; Level 1 (1–2) simple limited comment; Level 0 no marks. Structural features to consider include beginnings/endings, perspective shifts, paragraph-level topic changes, cohesion devices, sentence-level contributions to structure. Indicative content: establishing place/time to lull reader, time shifts (e.g. 'nine chimes') as signals of change, movement from single character to introduction of lamppost/man widening scope and adding tension, motif/repetition of 'glass' and 'glinting', use of interrogatives and rhetorical questions, chronological ordering vs shifts, use of short sharp declarative statements leading into dialogue, third-person narrative adding chilling tone, contrasts between imaginary and real town.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q4: Evaluation (To what extent do you agree?) — AO4
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on the second part of the Source. To what extent do you agree that the end part where the boy’s game comes to life takes a darker and more chilling tone? [20 marks]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked by levels: Level 4 (16–20) perceptive, detailed evaluation (evaluates effects on reader; perceptive understanding of writer’s methods; selects judicious range of textual detail; develops convincing critical response); Level 3 (11–15) clear relevant evaluation; Level 2 (6–10) some evaluation; Level 1 (1–5) simple limited evaluation; Level 0 no marks. Examiners should expect discussion of impressions of the boy’s game, evaluation of methods creating dark/chilling tone (pathetic fallacy, imagery, diction, verbs conveying panic like 'plunged' 'thundered', metaphor, onomatopoeia), and textual support. Indicative content includes themes of real v imaginary, what we learn about the boy, possible symbolism of the lamppost, moral/message, linguistic choices linked to evening/town/lamppost and striking imagery, contrast between innocence and darker ending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q5: Creative writing task — AO5 (Content & Organisation) and AO6 (Technical Accuracy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Either write a story about imaginative play (dark night image) or a story about a game that goes badly wrong. [40 marks total: 24 marks for content & organisation (AO5), 16 marks for technical accuracy (AO6)]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AO5 Content and Organisation is levelled: Level 4 (19–24) compelling/convincing (upper 22–24: register convincing and compelling for audience, assuredly matched to purpose, extensive and ambitious vocabulary, sustained crafting; organisation: varied/inventive structures, convincing complex ideas, fluently linked paragraphs). Level 3 (13–18) consistent/clear (range of effective structural features, engaging writing). Level 2 (7–12) some success (attempts to match register/purpose, some structural features). Level 1 (1–6) simple/limited. AO6 Technical Accuracy level descriptors: Level 4 (13–16) sentence demarcation consistently secure, wide range of punctuation used accurately, full range of sentence forms for effect, Standard English consistent with secure control of complex grammar, high accuracy of spelling including ambitious vocabulary; Level 3 (9–12) mostly accurate; Level 2 (5–8) some control; Level 1 (1–4) occasional demarcation and simple accuracy; Level 0 no marks if writing prevents understanding. Examiners should apply the split (24/16) when awarding marks and use level descriptors to allocate marks within each AO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicative content lists (examples to inform marking)
rubrics_metrics.description: For reading and evaluation questions, the mark scheme provides indicative content (examples of valid points, quotations, and interpretations) to illustrate the kinds of responses appropriate at each level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These lists are explicitly not exhaustive. Examiners should credit any valid interpretation or textual reference that meets the AO focus. Example indicative content for Q1 (possible points about the boy): he liked evening time the best; he felt able to slow time down; he felt in charge at the top of the mound; he didn’t want to go home/to bed; he collected pieces of broken green glass; he collected broken brown bottle necks; he played with the pieces of broken glass; he built little houses from the pieces of broken glass.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level award within a level (how to decide mark)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on deciding the specific mark once a level has been chosen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read back through the answer to clarify points and ensure the level and mark are appropriate. To award the top of a level, ensure all skills descriptors are met. A student at the bottom of a level will usually have met all descriptors of the previous level and at least one descriptor of the current level. Use exemplar indicative standards to judge whether responses meet descriptors for each level.

rubrics_metrics.name: No credit for verbatim copying (where applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Responses that copy the whole section of the text verbatim should not be credited marks where the task requires identification of specific information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verbatim copying does not show selection/interpretation and therefore cannot earn AO1 marks when the question requires identification of distinct points. Paraphrase is allowed and may be credited; paraphrases covering multiple points should be credited for each distinct point demonstrated.
